_comment: Hoodrich dealers -- the people you buy BULK from. Bulk cannot be sold until it has been
bagged up at the kitchen counter in the stash house.
TWO LISTS, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS READ. "dealers" is who you can actually buy off.
"later" is who you cannot, and nothing loads it -- it is a parking bay rather than a
disabled flag, so there is no half-live dealer in here waiting to be switched on by
something nobody remembers writing. Everything about a parked one is intact, down to the
last text message, and putting him back is moving his object out of "later" and into
"dealers". No rebuild.
Gerald and Tao are the whole trade at the moment. The gang corner dealers are parked
because their leaders are (leaders.json, same arrangement) and a corner man for a set you
cannot meet is a stranger selling you drugs for no reason; the independents are parked
with them so the catalogue opens up in one piece rather than a product at a time.
THE PROGRESSION: Gerald is where you start. Once you have moved enough weight
(Economy > DocksUnlockGrams in Hoodrich.ini, default 50g) he names the port, which is
what makes the dock worker -- and with him the whole catalogue at the best price -- exist
for you. Call him from the wheel and he drives out to you.
kind             Docks
drugs            what they sell. EMPTY means the whole catalogue -- that is the docks.
zones            GET_NAME_OF_ZONE codes they stand in
models           ped models tried IN ORDER; first one present in your install wins
priceMultiplier  applied to the wholesale price. Below 1.0 is a better deal.
openHour/closeHour  operating hours, 0-24. Wraps midnight when open > close.
greeting / buyLine / sourceReply / sourceTooSoon / farewell  what they say to you

afterCheng._comment: Who is stood on the dock after the old man is told about his son. Read through the same loader as the block above, so everything here means exactly what it means there. He is the opposite of Tao in every way that costs the player something: sober, on time, cheaper, and completely uninterested in you. The price is the reward and it has to actually BE one -- Tao already sells at the cheapest multiplier in the mod because he is the port, so anything at or above his number turns the old man's promise into a lie the player can check.

_purity: UNCUT, LIKE EVERYBODY WHO DRIVES IT TO YOU.
This was 0.75 and it was the only live entry that was not 1.0, which made 'anything
delivered arrives clean' true of two men out of three -- and a rule with an exception
in it is not a rule, it is a thing the player has to remember.
It holds because of WHAT THESE MEN ARE rather than because the delivery code forces
it: somebody who brings weight to your door is a supplier, and a supplier steps on
nothing, because his customers weigh it. Cutting happens further DOWN the chain --
your kitchen, your scales, and what you hand the man on the corner. The corner
dealers parked in 'later' still cut at 0.75, which is right: they are the bottom of
the chain and none of them drives anywhere.
So the strength quoted on the phone and the strength that lands in the stash are the
same number, and they are the same number for a reason rather than by being clamped.

_comment: HAO. NOT A SUPPLIER -- A CUSTOMER WHO HAPPENS TO HAVE SOME.
He is young, he is at every function in Los Santos, and he sells two things: pills and
tabs. That is not a product line, it is what a man who likes a night out has left over
-- which is why the ceiling is low and the price is high. You are not buying weight off
Hao. You are buying what is in his glovebox at a markup you would pay anyway, because
it is four in the morning and he is the one who answered.
NO SOFT. He had coke on the list to begin with and it is the one that did not fit: a man
with a bit of coke on him is dealing, and a man with a few pills and a sheet of tabs is
somebody who was going out anyway. The whole character of this entry is that he is not a
dealer, and the third product was quietly making him one.
DELIVERY ONLY, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF HOW HE WORKS. In person he is a car dealer --
his own lot, his own ped, his own conversation about motors, all in Locations/Hao.cs.
The pills are a phone number: you text him and he drives to you.
It used to be coordinates alone, with a comment here swearing nothing spawned a second
one. It did. HasSpot was true, so a dealer ped went down on the pin on top of the Hao
already standing there -- two of him, in two different shirts, each rolling his own
model -- and walking onto a forecourt got you a drug menu.
The coordinates below stay because they are still where he is. They just no longer mean
put a shop here.
UNCUT, and for him it is not a business decision. He did not step on it because he was
going to take it.
And he drives his own car to a delivery: the orange Penumbra off his own forecourt,
right down to the plate. See Locations/Hao.cs, which stamps the same seven letters on
the one parked outside.

_: OG VEE, AFTER THE BUY. He is not a plug you find on a corner and he is not a man you
meet -- he is the fella off the wall outside Leroy's Electrical, and the only way to
get his number is to do the job in the basement and drive away from it. Vernon.cs
opens him up once vernon_intro is done and the player has left Strawberry; the
introduction text then goes out through TextIfNewlyOpen like everybody else's.
ONE PRODUCT AND A GOOD PRICE, WHICH IS THE REWARD. He went to Rogers Scrap for a
kilo at twenty-two five and you are the reason he still has it, so he sells it on at
a number nobody else in the mod will do -- under the port, which is the cheapest
thing there was. What stops that being free money is the SIZE: two kilos a call. He
is a man with a basement, not a dock. Bulk still has to come off Tao.
deliveryOnly, so he is met where things actually happen rather than by walking up to
a corner he does not stand on. Same rule as Hao -- see DealerManager.HaveMet.
dealers._models: The man himself, and the cutscene copy behind him -- the same pair his wall uses, in the same order. He had NO models at all, and a dealer with no models is a delivery that cancels itself with 'nobody could make the run' every single time.
dealers.name: Vernon
dealers._lot: The door screen sizes his rows off lotValue, not maxOrderGrams: one lot is coke's five kilos scaled by lotValue over the port's hundred thousand, and the rows are that x1, x2 and x4. Ten thousand makes a lot five hundred grams, so the rows read 500g, 1kg and 2kg -- two kilos a call is the biggest thing on the list rather than a number nothing reads. Pure, because it is the same brick that came out of the yard; he passes it through, he does not step on it.
dealers._rides: His own Dorado, the one you rode to La Puerta in. It is the car the whole job happened in and the one parked down the side of the shop, so a delivery in anything else would be a stranger pulling up.
dealers._ride: The car parked down the side of the shop, to the bolt: gloss black over black, Benny's Originals with Lotta Chrome on them (wheel family 7, rim 16), dark smoke on the glass, green tubes underneath. Main builds the parked one from the same numbers.
dealers._stance: And how it sits: rear wheels tucked in a degree and a half, the back down fifteen centimetres, the nose up six. Held by the mod's own stance thread rather than a suspension slot, on the parked one and on the one he delivers in alike -- change it here and both change.

_cold: THE FIRST TIME, BEFORE THE VAGOS HAVE SQUARED YOU. Michael: 'make it so hes hostile
towards us in dialogue at first, but frank just wants to buy from him, so he will alow
the sale'. coldOpen, coldPush and coldGive are his; coldAsk, coldMoney and coldLeave are
what Franklin says back. The first buy squares you: truceLine and truceNote, and
